B.depoimento: I have ordered the construction of 2 spearman in Barcelona. My armies will march on the neutral villages of Tarragona and Girona to expand my territory and secure resources for the coming war.
B.plano: Attack Tarragona with spearman and Girona with knights. Build 2 spearman to reinforce Barcelona.

A.depoimento: I have ordered the capture of both neutral villages, sending spearmen and archers to Santarem and knights to Evora. I also began training a knight and an archer in my capital to rebuild my forces. With these villages secured, I will expand into the unknown territories.
A.plano: Capture Santarem and Evora to secure our borders and boost our economy. Next turn, use the newly built knight and archer at Lisboa to reinforce the forward villages or attack Coimbra and Faro. Begin building at the new villages as soon as they produce resources. Do not engage the enemy capital yet; focus on neutral territory.

A.depoimento: Our armies surged forward on three fronts, claiming Coimbra, Badajoz, and Faro for the crown. The spearman, archers, and knights fought with valor, securing new lands. We also fortified our heartlands by sending reinforcements to Santarem and building new archers in Lisboa.
A.plano: Attack Coimbra, Badajoz, and Faro to expand our territory and boost our economy. Build archers at Lisboa and send reinforcements to Santarem. Focus on neutral villages; do not engage the enemy capital yet.

B.depoimento: The knights ride out from Girona to claim Huesca for the crown! In Barcelona, the smiths forge new knights while our archers and spearmen march to strengthen Tarragona's defenses. The expansion begins!
B.plano: This turn: build 2 knights in Barcelona, 2 spearmen in Tarragona and Girona. Send 2 knights from Girona to attack Huesca. Send 2 spearmen and 1 archer from Barcelona to reinforce Tarragona. Next turn, attack Castellon with Tarragona's force. Keep an eye on enemy movements and defend our villages. Do not send to Zaragoza yet.

A.depoimento: We launched a successful assault on Sevilha with our archers from Badajoz, expanding our territory. We reinforced our northern frontier at Coimbra and southern flank at Evora, while building more archers to maintain our momentum.
A.plano: Conquer Sevilha to expand our territory to 7 villages. Reinforce Coimbra and Evora with archers and knights to prepare for attacks on Porto and Salamanca next turn. Build archers at Lisboa, Santarem, and Evora to increase our army.

B.depoimento: We are launching a coordinated attack on the neutral villages of Castellon and Zaragoza to secure our northern border and expand our territory. We are also reinforcing Huesca to serve as a staging ground for the next push into Pamplona. Our army is growing, and we are ready to claim what is ours.
B.plano: This turn: build 2 spearmen in Barcelona, Tarragona, and Girona. Send 3 spearmen from Tarragona to Castellon, 1 knight from Huesca to Zaragoza. Send 3 archers from Barcelona to Huesca, and 2 spearmen from Girona to Huesca to reinforce. Next turn, assess the situation; if Castellon and Zaragoza are captured, prepare to attack Pamplona from Huesca with the archers. Keep an eye on enemy movements and defend our villages. Do not send troops to unexplored areas yet.

A.depoimento: We launched an attack on Porto with our elite force from Coimbra, aiming to expand our territory northward. Simultaneously, we reinforced Badajoz with troops from Sevilha and Faro, preparing for the next push into Toledo. Our villages are bustling with activity as we build archers to grow our army. The conquest of Sevilha last turn has strengthened our southern border, and we are now ready to strike deeper into neutral territory.
A.plano: Attack Porto with Coimbra's full army to expand north. Reinforce Badajoz with Sevilha's archers and Faro's knights to prepare for an attack on Toledo next turn. Build archers in all villages to grow our army. Next turn, assess the situation after taking Porto and reinforce Coimbra further to push towards Salamanca.

A.depoimento: We are building archers and relocating them to the northern front to prepare for an attack on Vigo. Our non-archer troops are being consolidated in Coimbra and Badajoz. This will expand our territory and bring us closer to the enemy.
A.plano: Focus on building archers and moving them to Porto via Coimbra to attack Vigo. Also move spearmen and knights to Coimbra/Badajoz for safekeeping. Next turn, continue archer pipeline to Porto and assess strength for Vigo attack. Monitor enemy.

A.depoimento: I have ordered the construction of archers across all my domains and directed the movement of existing troops towards the front lines. Reinforcements from Coimbra are marching to Porto to bolster the attack on Vigo, while forces from Badajoz and Faro are converging on Sevilha to prepare for the assault on Cordoba. My aim is to expand my territory and increase my village count.
A.plano: Building archers in all villages. Sending reinforcements from Coimbra to Porto to prepare for attack on Vigo. Also moving troops to Sevilha to prepare for Cordoba attack. Next turn, assess the gathered forces and launch attacks on Vigo and Cordoba. Keep an eye on enemy movements.

B.depoimento: This turn, we marched from Huesca to Pamplona with spearmen and archers, and sent a knight from Zaragoza as reinforcement. We also moved troops from Tarragona and Barcelona to Zaragoza, and from Girona to Huesca to prepare for future attacks. We built new troops in all our villages to grow our army.
B.plano: Next turn: Check if Pamplona captured. Send troops from Zaragoza to attack Madrid (need spearmen to counter knights). Send from Castellon to attack Valencia (need archers). Reinforce Huesca with Girona's troops for further expansion. Build more troops.

A.depoimento: I ordered the archers from Porto and Sevilha to strike Vigo and Cordoba, hoping to capture these neutral villages and expand my territory. I also ordered the construction of archers across all my villages and sent knights to reinforce the front lines.
A.plano: Attacking Vigo and Cordoba with archers from Porto and Sevilha to capture these neutral villages. Building archers in all villages to grow the army. Sending knights from Coimbra and Badajoz to reinforce Porto and Sevilha for the next phase of expansion. Next turn, assess the results of the attacks and prepare to push into Burgos and Murcia.

B.depoimento: Pamplona should fall this turn as Huesca's 3 archers arrive — spearman-counter bonus gives 12 effective attack vs 8 defense. I committed Zaragoza's entire force to Madrid: 8 spearmen with the knight-counter multiplier should overwhelm the 4-knight garrison. Tarragona's troops march to Castellon to build the hammer needed for Valencia next turn. Building 2 spearmen in all six villages — our army grows by 12 this turn alone. The west remains unexplored; once Madrid drops, the road to Lisboa opens.
B.plano: Madrid attack: 8 spearmen + 1 archer should win with 1.5x knight-counter (15 effective vs 10 defense). Valencia waits — Castellon alone can't beat defense 8, so Tarragona's 4 spearmen + 2 archers arrive first. Check Pamplona result. After Madrid falls, explore west to Salamanca [7] and Burgos [14]. Keep building 2 spearmen per village.

A.depoimento: We struck at Murcia with archers, capturing the southern neutral. Our spearmen gather for the northern push, while our knights prepare to strike at Burgos. The weak walls of Evora and Sevilha are reinforced.
A.plano: Attack Murcia with archers from Cordoba. Build spearmen for Salamanca/Toledo and archers for reinforcement. Reinforce Evora and Sevilha. Gather spearmen at Coimbra and knight at Vigo. Next turn, assess and continue building.

A.depoimento: My armies took Salamanca and Burgos, while reinforcements rushed to Badajoz and Murcia. The enemy remains hidden in the east, but my net is closing in.
A.plano: This turn I conquer Salamanca and Burgos, and reinforce Badajoz and Murcia for attacks on Toledo and Valencia next turn. I must remember to rebuild troops in Coimbra, Sevilha, and Vigo after sending them. Next turn, after seeing Madrid, I will plan the push into enemy territory.

B.depoimento: I am gathering my armies at Castellon to strike Valencia. I have built archers in my eastern villages and sent my troops to reinforce Castellon. In the north, I am preparing attacks on Teruel and Burgos by building the appropriate counter units.
B.plano: Next turn: Castellon will have 11 spearman and 7 archer. Attack Valencia with 7 archers and 4 spearmen for counter bonus. Zaragoza will have 8 spearmen; prepare to attack Teruel. Huesca will have 2 knights; send them to Madrid to start Burgos attack. Do not attack Valencia from multiple villages; use Castellon as the sole attack origin to concentrate force.

A.depoimento: My forces have successfully conquered Burgos and are now launching a multi-pronged offensive. Salamanca, Toledo, Valencia, and Pamplona are all under simultaneous attack. By nightfall, I expect to add four more villages to my domain, bringing the total to 16. The path to the enemy capital is opening, but first I must secure Madrid.
A.plano: Conquer Salamanca, Toledo, Valencia, and Pamplona this turn to reach 16 villages. Next turn, reinforce Salamanca and Toledo, then launch a double attack on Madrid. Rebuild troops in Coimbra, Sevilha, and Vigo to maintain momentum. Do not attack Madrid this turn as it is too strong.

B.depoimento: My armies attacked on three fronts. The archers from Castellon stormed Teruel, while spearmen and archers took Valencia. From Zaragoza, knights and archers fell upon Pamplona. A small force from Madrid raided Burgos. Reinforcements from the interior marched to the borders. The enemy's response will determine the next moves.
B.plano: Check if Burgos fell; if not, reinforce Madrid. If Teruel taken, send spearman to hold it. If Valencia taken, explore Murcia. If Pamplona taken, consider attack on Vigo or Burgos. Build more troops as resources allow.

A.depoimento: Turn 13 is a turn of consolidation and preparation. I have ordered the construction of troops across all my villages to maximize my army. The elite knight and archer force from Vigo is marching to capture the enemy village of Burgos. Simultaneously, I am reinforcing my northern front by sending troops from Porto and Coimbra to Salamanca, and from Badajoz to Toledo. In the south, Cordoba's troops are marching to Murcia to set up a major offensive against Valencia. I am confident that these moves will bring me closer to victory.
A.plano: Focus on capturing Burgos [14] with Vigo's army. Reinforce Salamanca [7] and Toledo [8] to prepare for attacks on Madrid [12] and Teruel [13]. Consolidate forces in the south (Murcia [15]) to threaten Valencia [16]. Build troops across all villages to maintain economic and military growth. Do not attack Madrid yet; wait for reinforcements from Porto and Coimbra to arrive at Salamanca.

B.depoimento: Our armies strike on three fronts: Valencia assaults Murcia, Burgos raids Vigo, Madrid marches on Salamanca. Reinforcements from the interior flow to the borders. We build spearmen and archers to feed the war.
B.plano: Verify conquests of Murcia, Vigo, Salamanca. Send troops to hold and explore next: Cordoba, Porto, Coimbra. If any attack failed, regroup. Build more troops. Watch for enemy counterattacks on Valencia, Madrid, Burgos.

A.depoimento: I am coordinating a multi-front expansion. Toledo is taking the neutral village of Teruel. In the south, Sevilha is moving to Cordoba to launch an attack on Murcia next turn. In the north, I am reinforcing Vigo for defense while massing troops in Salamanca and Toledo for the eventual assault on Madrid. My economy is growing with new builds in every village.
A.plano: Take Teruel with Toledo's army. Reinforce Cordoba from Sevilha to prepare for Murcia next turn. Reinforce Vigo from Porto for defense against Burgos. Massively reinforce Salamanca with knights from Lisboa and Santarem to attack Madrid next turn. Reinforce Toledo with knights from Evora and Badajoz, and spearmen from Faro, for the push north. Build troops across all villages.

B.depoimento: This turn we launched an attack on Vigo, reinforced our borders, and built up our armies. The enemy's attempt to reinforce Salamanca was noted, but we are prepared. Our forces are gathering for the next push.
B.plano: Attacking Vigo this turn with Burgos troops. Reinforced Madrid from Zaragoza and Huesca; reinforced Burgos from Pamplona; reinforced Murcia from Valencia. Built troops in all villages. Next turn: attack Salamanca from Madrid, Cordoba from Murcia, and follow up on Vigo. Watch for enemy counterattacks.

A.depoimento: This turn, my forces strike on two fronts. Cordoba's army marches on Murcia, while Teruel's troops head for Castellon. I am reinforcing my key border villages—Toledo, Teruel, Vigo, and Salamanca—to secure my gains and prepare for the inevitable push towards Madrid. The enemy's capital remains my ultimate target, but I will take their outlying villages first to reach the 18-victory threshold.
A.plano: Attack Murcia from Cordoba and Castellon from Teruel. Reinforce Toledo, Teruel, Vigo, Cordoba, and Salamanca to prepare for the next wave of attacks on Madrid and Burgos. Build troops across all villages to maintain momentum.

B.depoimento: Teruel and Vigo both fall this turn - two borders reclaimed. Valencia and Burgos both empty their garrisons for the assault, so I'm rushing reinforcements in from Pamplona, Tarragona, and Huesca to hold the line. The enemy's Salamanca army keeps growing, but I'm going around it. Building knights in the rear for the next push toward Toledo and Porto.
B.plano: This turn: Valencia→Teruel (10 troops, keep 1 spear), Burgos→Vigo (all 6), Pamplona→Burgos, Tarragona→Castellon (3 knights), Huesca→Zaragoza (7). Build everywhere. Enemy army marching to Toledo - don't engage there yet. Watch for enemy counterattacks on Valencia/Castellon/Zaragoza from Teruel. Next: attack Toledo from Teruel, Porto from Vigo, reinforce Teruel.

B.depoimento: Cordoba falls today to Murcia's assault, carrying me to 13 villages. I march Zaragoza's veterans to Madrid to shield the capital from Salamanca's growing host, while Burgos gathers for Vigo and Teruel braces for Toledo. Every village raises a knight — the realm arms for the push to 18.
B.plano: Murcia→Cordoba (all 8) takes the weakest enemy village. Zaragoza→Madrid (all 21) shields the capital from Salamanca. Madrid→Burgos (3s/1a/1k)+Pamplona→Burgos (1k) for Vigo next turn. Valencia→Teruel (3s)+Castellon→Teruel (2k) hold vs Toledo. Build 1 knight per village + 2 spearman Teruel. Next: Burgos→Vigo, Madrid→Toledo (7 archer+7 knight, counter bonus x1.5), Cordoba→Sevilha. Watch Salamanca→Madrid.

A.depoimento: I ordered a swift attack on the weakly defended Murcia [15] with archers from Cordoba [11]. I am reinforcing Cordoba and Toledo to prepare for further expansion into enemy territory. All my villages are busy building troops to strengthen our borders.
A.plano: Attack Murcia [15] with 2 archers from Cordoba [11] to capture it. Reinforce Cordoba with troops from Toledo [8] and Sevilha [9] for the next turn. Build up all villages to maximize troop production. Do not attack Madrid [12] or Burgos [14] yet as they are too strong.

B.depoimento: Launch a multi-front assault: Madrid's archers and knights crush Toledo with the counter bonus, Burgos's full army takes Vigo, and Valencia reinforces Murcia for Cordoba next turn. Building knights in every village to sustain the offensive toward 18 villages.
B.plano: Madrid→Toledo (12a+12k, counter x1.5, attack 108 vs 40). Burgos→Vigo (all 27 vs 18). Valencia→Murcia (1k) for Cordoba next turn. Zaragoza→Madrid (1k) reinforce. Build 1 knight per village + 1 archer Murcia. Next: Murcia→Cordoba (2k+1a), Vigo→Porto, Toledo→Badajoz. Watch Salamanca.

A.depoimento: This turn, King A's forces struck on three fronts: Vigo took the weakly defended Burgos, Cordoba captured Murcia, and Salamanca's mighty army assaulted Madrid. We also moved troops to reinforce our vulnerable border villages of Badajoz and Cordoba, and rebuilt our ranks with new constructions. The kingdom expands.
A.plano: We attacked Burgos, Murcia, and Madrid to expand our territory. Reinforcements were sent to Badajoz and Cordoba to defend against enemy attacks. Salamanca was reinforced after sending its main force. Next turn, we must check the outcomes of these battles, especially whether we held Badajoz and Cordoba. Continue building troops and plan next attacks on Huesca or Pamplona. Do not neglect border defense.

B.depoimento: Toledo is mine at last! Now I strike Badajoz with its garrison while rushing reinforcements from Madrid and Teruel to hold Toledo against the enemy's counterattack. Building knights across the entire realm to field overwhelming armies for the next pushes on all fronts.
B.plano: Toledo→Badajoz (9a+9k, attack 54 vs defense 10). Madrid→Toledo (10s+3k) and Teruel→Toledo (9s+2a+4k) to reinforce against the enemy army arriving at Toledo. Pamplona→Burgos (2k) to build up for Vigo capture next turn. Build 1 knight per village + archers where iron is short. Next turn: Vigo from Burgos, Cordoba from Toledo/Murcia, watch Salamanca.

A.depoimento: Turn 19 is the turn we strike hard! We are sending all available forces from our borders to crush the weak enemy villages of Pamplona, Zaragoza, Murcia, and Badajoz. Our scouts report that these villages are lightly defended, and with our superior tactics and counter bonuses, we expect to conquer them all simultaneously. This will bring us to 16 villages, putting us ever closer to the 75% needed to claim victory! We are also building knights across our empire to ensure our armies remain strong and fast.
A.plano: We are launching a multi-pronged offensive to conquer Pamplona, Zaragoza, Murcia, and Badajoz. This will bring our total to 16 villages. We are leaving Toledo alone for now due to its heavy defenses and potential enemy reinforcements. We are building knights in almost all our villages to maintain a strong mobile force for next turn's pushes, including towards the enemy capital. We must be careful not to leave Salamanca completely undefended, so we are leaving one archer there while sending the rest to Badajoz.

A.depoimento: Our armies converge on Valencia and Teruel. Valencia is taken tomorrow, Teruel the day after. Reinforcements pour in to secure our borders. The enemy capital may fall eventually, but we win by holding 18 villages.
A.plano: We are taking Valencia on turn 21 with a strong force from Murcia, leaving 1 knight for defense. We are sending all 4 spearman from Zaragoza to Teruel; they arrive turn 22. We reinforce Zaragoza with 5 archers and 2 knights from Madrid, and build 4 spearman there. We reinforce Pamplona with Burgos' troops and build archers/knights. We reinforce Badajoz with Salamanca's troops and build spear/archers. We build knights in interior villages for mobility. Hold new villages for 2 turns to win.

A.depoimento: Our spearmen have conquered Teruel, bringing our total to 18 villages! We are reinforcing Teruel with Zaragoza's archers and knights, and sending Valencia's troops to conquer Castellon to push our count to 19. Madrid is reinforcing Zaragoza to keep our northern front strong. We are building troops across the empire to ensure our dominance. The path to victory is clear!
A.plano: We are conquering Teruel this turn with the 4 spearmen already marching. We reinforce Teruel with 5 archers and 2 knights from Zaragoza to hold it against counterattacks. We conquer Castellon with Valencia's troops to secure a second village and reach 19 villages. We reinforce Zaragoza with Madrid's troops to prevent enemy encirclement. We build knights and archers across all villages to grow our army and secure our borders. Hold the new villages for 2 consecutive turns to win.

B.depoimento: This turn, we rushed knights to Teruel to bolster its defense against the incoming enemy army, while simultaneously striking at Cordoba with a lightning force. Our northern villages sent reinforcements to Tarragona and Huesca. We continue to build knights across our realm to maintain our war machine.
B.plano: Check if Teruel holds against enemy attack. If Cordoba captured, send reinforcements and build there. Next, target Murcia or Sevilha. Watch for enemy counterattacks.

A.depoimento: This turn we stand firm and prepare. Our columns of knights and archers march from the quiet interior to the restless borders, reinforcing every vulnerable village until they stand like iron. The forges of our cities burn bright as we churn out a fresh host of knights and archers. We hold our swords still for now, letting our defenses grow, knowing that next turn we will strike hard and take the village we need to claim victory.
A.plano: This turn we focus entirely on defense and consolidation. We are marching knights and archers from interior villages to reinforce our border villages, creating a nearly impregnable defensive line. We are not attacking this turn to avoid unnecessary losses and to allow our builders to produce a large number of new knights and archers. Next turn, we will launch a decisive attack on a weak enemy village (likely Cordoba or Huesca) with overwhelming force to finally reach 18 villages. We must then hold that village for two consecutive turns to win. Our borders are now extremely strong, and the enem

A.depoimento: Our armies launch a decisive assault on Cordoba, the weakest enemy village. We have sent overwhelming force from Sevilha and Badajoz, while Valencia prepares to reinforce. Our borders are strengthened against any counterattack. We are one step closer to victory!
A.plano: We are attacking Cordoba this turn with forces from Sevilha and Badajoz to capture our 18th village. We are sending reinforcements from Valencia to hold it next turn, and reinforcing our border villages to prevent enemy advances. Next turn, we must hold Cordoba for the second consecutive turn to win. We will continue building knights and archers to maintain our strength.

A.depoimento: This turn, we fortified our borders and secured our newly conquered village of Cordoba. We sent massive reinforcements to Castellon and Pamplona to shield them from enemy attacks, while building troops across our entire empire. Our army is now fully prepared to defend the 18 villages and claim victory!
A.plano: We are focusing on defending our 18 villages to secure the 2 consecutive turns victory. We heavily reinforced Cordoba, Castellon, Pamplona, and Zaragoza. We built troops across all villages to maximize our defense and counter the enemy's knights with spearmen. Next turn, we must verify that we still hold all 18 villages and that Cordoba has held for 2 turns to win the game.

B.depoimento: My forces struck with lightning speed, capturing three enemy villages in one turn. While the enemy was distracted reinforcing distant cities, we seized Castellon, Valencia, and Pamplona. Reinforcements are already marching to secure our gains.
B.plano: Next turn: move newly built knights to the front. Use captured Castellon to launch further attacks. Reinforce Tarragona and Huesca with the troops sent this turn. Keep an eye on enemy movements toward Zaragoza and Cordoba.

B.depoimento: Our knights surge forth to conquer Murcia, Pamplona, and Castellon. Reinforcements strengthen our borders. We build a balanced army to prepare for the next phase of the campaign.
B.plano: Send knights to attack Murcia, Pamplona, and Castellon. Reinforce Huesca from Girona. Build archers to counter Zaragoza's spearmen. Do not attack Zaragoza yet; we need more archers. Keep an eye on enemy movements.

B.depoimento: Last turn we seized Murcia, Pamplona, and Castellon. Today our Pamplonian cavalry storms Burgos to widen our realm. Across the north we are mustering archers at Huesca for the decisive blow at Zaragoza, the crossroads of the map. Reinforcements ride to Murcia and Huesca to keep our borders solid.
B.plano: Order: 4 knights from Pamplona to attack Burgos [14]. Send Valencia's 2 spears + 1 knight to Murcia [15] and Girona's full team to Huesca [20]. Build archers in every northern village plus Teruel; build knights in Castellon, Valencia, Toledo, Murcia. Do not attack Zaragoza until Huesca holds 8+ archers with knight support. Guard Pamplona and Murcia from enemy counterattacks.

A.depoimento: I launched a massive four-front offensive today, targeting the weakest points of King B's empire. My armies from Badajoz, Madrid, Cordoba, and Zaragoza marched simultaneously to take Toledo, Burgos, Murcia, and Tarragona. With superior numbers and careful troop composition, I expect to crush the enemy defenses and expand my kingdom to 17 villages by dawn.
A.plano: Conquer Toledo, Burgos, Murcia, and Tarragona this turn to reach 17 villages. Next turn, attack Pamplona and Teruel from Zaragoza to reach 19 villages and secure the win. Rebuild troops in all villages to maintain momentum and defend the new borders.

B.depoimento: We launched a major assault on Zaragoza with all of Huesca's might, sending 18 troops to break the enemy hub. Simultaneously, we reinforced Huesca with archers from Girona and Pamplona to hold the line. In the east, we sent knights from Barcelona to Tarragona and from Castellon and Valencia to Teruel to strengthen our borders. We built archers and knights across our realm, focusing on Huesca, Burgos, and other key villages to fuel the next phase of the campaign.
B.plano: Check if Zaragoza fell. If yes, move troops from Huesca to Zaragoza and prepare attack on Madrid. If no, reassess Huesca's losses and rebuild. Watch for enemy counterattacks on Huesca, Tarragona, Teruel, and Burgos. Keep an eye on Vigo - it's weak and may be taken next turn. Ensure all border villages have enough troops.

A.depoimento: I conquered Valencia and Pamplona, bringing my total to 18 villages. I also reinforced my border villages and rebuilt my armies. I must now hold these villages for one more turn to secure victory.
A.plano: Attack Valencia and Pamplona to reach 18 villages. Reinforce borders and rebuild forces. Next turn, hold new villages and watch for enemy counterattacks. Consider attacking Zaragoza to link Tarragona.

B.depoimento: Our knights ride from Teruel to seize Valencia. Archers from Huesca march to Zaragoza, strengthening our northern stronghold. Every forge burns day and night as we build a mighty army. The enemy's time is ending!
B.plano: This turn: send 10 knights from Teruel to Valencia; send 3 archers from Huesca to Zaragoza. Build 2 knights in Teruel, 1k+1a in Huesca, 3a in Zaragoza, 1k+2a in Castellon, 2k in Barcelona, 1k+2a in Girona. Next turn, attack Tarragona from Zaragoza with the reinforced army. Defend Huesca and other borders.

A.depoimento: I am launching a decisive strike on Valencia from Murcia to push our village count to 18 and secure the win. I am reinforcing our border villages with interior troops and building knights across the realm to prepare for the next phase of the campaign.
A.plano: Attack Valencia [16] from Murcia [15] with all available troops to conquer it and reach the 18-village threshold for victory. Reinforce Murcia with Cordoba's troops, Madrid with Salamanca's, Pamplona with Burgos', and Toledo with Badajoz' to secure the borders after the attack. Build 2 knights in every village to rapidly expand our military might. Hold the rest of the line and watch for enemy counter-moves.

B.depoimento: This turn we launched a major assault on Tarragona with Zaragoza's archers and knights. We reinforced our positions by moving troops from Girona to Huesca and from Huesca to Zaragoza. We also sent part of Teruel's force to Valencia to prepare for the attack on Murcia. Our villages continue to produce archers and knights to grow our might.
B.plano: Next turn: attack Murcia from Valencia. Attack Madrid from Zaragoza/Tarragona. Build more troops. Defend Huesca and other borders. Keep an eye on Tarragona's defense after we take it.
